hv6: ssMOOD (spatial and single-cell Major depression disease Omics Online Database) is a comprehensive database focused on depression research, integrating single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics data from humans and mice. It aims to provide high-quality resources and interactive analysis tools for multidimensional depression studies.
hv8: The data are mainly derived from mouse and human samples, covering two types of sequencing data: single-cell transcriptomics and spatial transcriptomics.
hv10-1: Utilizes an efficient plotting engine and data structure to support real-time loading and smooth interaction with large-scale data.
hv10-2: Provides multiple chart types, including UMAP clustering plots, Spatial location map, heatmaps, and more.
hv10-3: Users can freely explore the data through interactive operations such as zooming, filtering, and hover tooltips, with support for conditional filtering, cell type highlighting, and multi-plot linked analysis.
hv12: Provides two types of integrated datasets, covering single-cell transcriptomics (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) data, integrated by experimental conditions and anatomical regions.
home_hero_sub: A spatial and single-cell Major Depression Omics Online Database — integrating multi-modal transcriptomics across human and mouse brain tissue at cellular resolution.
home_hero_tagline: Mapping MDD at cellular resolution · BA12 · BA46 · PFC · ACC
home_repo_sub: Four integrated modalities across species and platforms
home_mdd_title: Decoding Major Depressive Disorder at cellular resolution
home_mdd_body: MDD is a common neuropsychiatric disorder and a major contributor to disability worldwide, yet its cellular and molecular underpinnings remain poorly understood. By integrating spatial transcriptomics with single-cell RNA-seq, ssMOOD enables researchers to map gene expression changes to specific cell types and anatomical regions.
home_mdd_stat2_l: Major contributor to global disability burden
home_mdd_feat1_desc: Identify dysregulated neuron subtypes, microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes in MDD.
home_mdd_feat2_desc: Preserve anatomical context to map MDD gene gradients across cortical layers.
home_mdd_feat3_desc: Parallel human and mouse datasets for translational biomarker validation.
home_tech_stereo_desc: Stereo-seq is a high-resolution spatial transcriptomics technology that preserves tissue coordinates together with gene expression. The spatial transcriptomics samples in ssMOOD are mainly based on this technology.
home_tech_snrna_desc: snRNA-seq profiles RNA from isolated nuclei, making it suitable for frozen or difficult-to-dissociate brain tissue and for resolving cell types and states.
home_tech_10x_desc: 10x Genomics is a widely used single-cell omics platform for high-throughput capture of cells or nuclei and generation of expression matrices. Some ssMOOD single-cell data use this platform.
home_tech_snatac_desc: snATAC-seq measures chromatin accessibility at single-nucleus resolution, supporting analysis of regulatory elements and cell-type-specific accessibility changes.
home_tech_gwas_desc: GWAS Catalog curates published genome-wide association studies and links traits with variants and genes. ssMOOD uses GWAS trait information to connect genetic associations with cell-level results.
home_tech_scdrs_desc: scDRS projects disease- or trait-associated gene signals onto single-cell data to estimate cell-level disease relevance scores and test cell-type enrichment.
home_tech_seurat_desc: Seurat is a common R framework for single-cell analysis, including quality control, dimensionality reduction, clustering, integration, and differential analysis.
home_tech_scanpy_desc: Scanpy is a Python framework for single-cell analysis, suited for large expression matrices and common workflows such as dimensionality reduction, clustering, and visualization.
home_tech_squidpy_desc: Squidpy is a Python toolkit for spatial omics data, supporting spatial neighborhoods, spatial autocorrelation, and tissue-structure analysis.
home_tech_deseq2_desc: DESeq2 is an RNA-seq differential expression tool that uses negative binomial models to estimate expression changes and statistical significance.
home_tech_harmony_desc: Harmony is a batch-correction and data-integration method commonly used to reduce technical differences across samples, batches, or platforms.
bsc2: In the single-cell module of ssMOOD, datasets include single-cell data from both humans and mice. As of July 2026, the database contains 938,615 cells. The datasets provide detailed cell type annotations and complete gene expression information, enabling cross-species comparisons and studies on cellular heterogeneity.
bst2: The ssMOOD spatial transcriptomics (Stereo-seq) module provides data from over 5 million cells, mainly from mice and including human samples. Powered by high-resolution Stereo-seq technology, it enables the analysis of single-cell spatial locations and gene expression, supports cross-species studies, and is equipped with rich tools and a user-friendly interface to facilitate spatial omics research.

browse_hub_sub: ssMOOD integrates multi-modal omics across human and mouse cortex. Choose a modality below to explore datasets and follow future data and analysis updates.
browse_hub_sc_desc: snRNA-seq across mouse cortex (layers I–V) and human dlPFC (BA9, BA11, BA12, BA46). Per-cell transcriptomic profiles with cell-type annotation.
browse_hub_st_desc: Stereo-seq spatial maps preserving tissue architecture. Per-spot gene expression mapped to anatomical coordinates.
browse_hub_atac_desc: Chromatin accessibility at single-cell resolution. Identifies cell-type-specific regulatory regions and TF binding sites altered in MDD.
browse_hub_gwas_desc: Trait-level genetic associations linked to cell types, brain regions, conditions, and scDRS cell-score summaries.

browse_hub_methylation_when: Refining search, visualization, and downstream analysis

browse_hub_roadmap_desc: Future updates will prioritize validated public datasets, cross-species comparison, and multi-omics analysis capabilities. Specific modules will be released after data curation and quality control are complete.
